name: Commercial Bank (Qatar)
founded: 1974 (incorporated under Emiri Decree No. 73 of 1974, commercial registration no. 150; markets itself as Qatar's first private bank)
ownership_summary: QSE-listed private-sector bank. At 31 Dec 2025 Qatar Holding LLC held 16.3% and no other individual or entity held more than 5%; Qatari holders owned 72.0% and foreign investors 28.0% (Corporate Governance Report 2025). The Articles cap any holder other than QIA/Qatar Holding (or a GDR depositary) below 5%. Foreign ownership limit raised to 100% in March 2022.
government_link: Yes - Qatar Holding LLC (QIA subsidiary) is the only holder above 5%, with 16.3% at 31 Dec 2025 (S7). The original research figure of 21.3% total government ownership was not found in the sources checked.
group_structure: The Commercial Bank (P.S.Q.C.) is the QSE-listed parent. Fully owned subsidiaries (FY2025 note 1): Alternatifbank A.S. (Turkey, banking; hyperinflation accounting), Commercial Bank Financial Services L.L.C. (CBFS, QSE brokerage, QFMA-regulated), CB Asset Management L.L.C. (CBAM, QFCRA licence 01179, 'Wealth Management'), CBQ Finance Limited (Bermuda, debt issuance), CB Global Trading Limited (Cayman, financial services), CB Innovation Services L.L.C. (operations/technology captive), CB Leasing Company L.L.C., CB Real Estate Properties L.L.C., and Sondook Fund LLC (a money market fund launched in 2025, managed and consolidated by the Group, with QAR 50m of external units shown as non-controlling interests at 31 Dec 2025). Associates: National Bank of Oman SAOG (34.9%) and United Arab Bank PJSC (39.9% per CBQ statements; 39.91% per UAB's Annual Report 2025, profiled separately as ae-uab and equity-accounted here, so UAB figures must not be added to CBQ's). Joint venture: Massoun Insurance Services L.L.C. (50%, insurance brokerage).

subsidiaries.activity: Banking (UAE) - associate. CBQ statements round to 39.9% after the 2025 rights issue (from 40.0%); 39.91% at 31 Dec 2025 per UAB Annual Report 2025 as recorded in ae-uab.

footprint: Qatar: distribution network of 28 locations (branches, CB Premium Lounges and self-service points) and 313 ATMs in 2025 (Annual Report 2025 p.31; p.4 says 27 locations). Turkey via Alternatif Bank. Strategic associates in Oman (NBO) and the UAE (UAB) form the bank's 'alliance' network.
customer_segments: Retail: mass and expatriate salary customers (CB@Work employee banking), cards, remittances; affluent (CB Premium Sadara) and private (CB Premium Private, invitation only); Qatari nationals as a 2026-2030 growth priority. Wholesale: GREs and government, large and mid-corporates, SMEs (20,000+ active SME customers in 2025), international corporates and financial institutions, and ultra-high-net-worth family offices outside Qatar via International Banking.
business_lines: Segments (FY2025 note 6): Qatar Wholesale Banking (credit, deposits, FX, derivatives, syndication; also manages money market funds and the proprietary investment portfolio), Qatar Retail Banking (accounts, cards, consumer, vehicle and mortgage loans, custodial services, wealth management, and brokerage through CBFS), International (Alternatif Bank; associates NBO and UAB) and Unallocated/other. Wealth Management sits in Retail and offers advisory, third-party mutual funds, International Investment Plans, fixed income (bonds and sukuk), structured solutions and share trading (CBFS for QSE, CB Alpha Trader for US, UK, Europe and Hong Kong). CBAM is the QFC-licensed asset manager. Treasury and Investments covers ALM, proprietary investments and treasury sales. H1 2026 net operating income QAR 2,459.4m.

capabilities.wealth_summary: CBQ runs wealth inside Retail Banking under EGM Shahnawaz Rashid. Premium tiers are CB Premium Sadara (affluent; Qatari salary of QAR 25,000 or expat salary of QAR 35,000 plus loans/deposits of QAR 365,000) and CB Premium Private (by invitation), served from CB Premium Lounges. The wealth advisory runs a four-step process with risk profiling on a 1-5 scale. The product shelf has third-party mutual funds from Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock and Kotak (from USD 3,000), International Investment Plans (regular saving from USD 300 a month), local and global bonds and sukuk, and structured solutions. Clients can trade QSE shares through the CBFS subsidiary (CB Waseet app, Trade Direct) and US, UK, European and Hong Kong shares through CB Alpha Trader. In 2025 the bank added investment account opening and wealth services to the CBQ Mobile App, and its CB Asset Management subsidiary (QFCRA-licensed) launched the Sondook money market fund. The 2026-2030 strategy targets affluent and private Qatari clients and 'expansion of digital wealth tools and solutions'. CBQ was named Best Wealth Management Bank in Qatar at the TAB Global Middle East Awards 2026. It discloses no wealth AUM.

segments.name: CB Premium Sadara
segments.eligibility: Qataris: minimum monthly salary transfer QAR 25,000; expats: QAR 35,000; and total loans and/or deposits of QAR 365,000. Existing customers upgrading: expat salary QAR 50,000, Qatari QAR 25,000 plus additional products. At bank's discretion.

segments.name: CB Premium Private (Premium Private Banking)
segments.eligibility: By invitation only; no published threshold (application form salary bands start at QAR 25,000).

private_banking.detail: CB Premium Private: invitation-only service with a dedicated private banker, a tailored approach, and meetings with industry-specific financial experts; covers deposits, credit, mortgages, insurance, wealth management, investments and brokerage. Clients are served from CB Premium Lounges. International Banking also serves ultra-high-net-worth family offices outside Qatar. The 2026-2030 strategy prioritises affluent and Private Banking Qatari clients.

asset_management.detail: CB Asset Management L.L.C. (CBAM): wholly owned, capital QAR 50m, QFCRA licence 01179 for investment management, advisory and fund management. It is led by Faisal Qamar Khan with Kamal Farhat as deputy. The group launched and consolidates the Sondook Fund LLC money market fund (2025; QAR 50m of group units plus QAR 50m of external units at 31 Dec 2025), shown on the website as the 'CBAM Sondook Fund'. The website also carries documents for an in-house 'Al Waseela' fund (not reviewed). CBFS has its own Head of Asset Management. No AUM is disclosed.

brokerage.detail: Commercial Bank Financial Services L.L.C. (CBFS): wholly owned, QFMA-regulated. Offers QSE securities trading, margin trading, liquidity provision, Trade Direct online trading, phone trading, a dedicated brokers' lounge and the CB Waseet mobile app (biometric login, instant transfers to CBQ accounts). It began market-making in 2025. International share trading runs through the bank's CB Alpha Trader platform.

digital_investing.detail: CB Alpha Trader (desktop and iOS/Android): trade US, UK, European and Hong Kong markets; the account is opened and funded instantly through internet/mobile banking; 60-day demo account; lower fees announced on the current page; used for the Aug 2026 Young Investors simulation. CB Waseet app for QSE trading through CBFS. The CBQ Mobile App added investment account opening and wealth services in 2025, plus a CB Video Relationship Manager. App NPS is 86. Technology vendor for Alpha Trader not disclosed.

advisory.detail: Accredited, bilingual Wealth Advisors follow a four-step process: financial review, risk profiling (1 Risk Averse to 5 Aggressive), portfolio construction and execution, and periodic review/rebalancing. The Annual Report 2025 cites in-house research, thematic portfolios and tailored advisory.

discretionary.detail: CBAM holds a QFCRA investment management licence, but no discretionary mandate product for retail or private clients is published. The wealth pages describe advisory portfolios with rebalancing discussions.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: The Annual Report 2025 mentions 'thematic portfolios' within advisory, and a 2023 interview said AI-based robo-advisory tools were in development. No live robo or model-portfolio product was found on the website.

funds_platform.detail: Third-party mutual funds from Fidelity International, Franklin Templeton, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock and Kotak (lump sum from USD 3,000 / QAR 10,000), with a published mutual fund catalogue. International Investment Plans (SIP) start at USD 300 plus USD 300 a month. The Annual Report 2025 cites 'strategic distribution partnerships with leading global asset managers'. Platform or custody provider not named.

structured_products.detail: 'Structured Solutions': bespoke notes on equities, indices and commodities from A-rated issuers (issuers not named), with varying capital protection.

private_markets.detail: The website product list includes 'Alternative Investments' (content not reviewed). CBQ has distributed CB Leasing and Finance Funds with WCP Investments (second fund launched Dec 2019; seen in search results only). No current private equity or private credit offer was confirmed.

islamic_wealth.detail: Conventional bank. Its fixed income shelf includes sukuk, and it launched a Shariah-compliant global multi-asset fund managed by Franklin Templeton in 2023 (release seen in search results only).

initiatives.what: Relaunched the Sadara affluent proposition with a new Sadara Visa Infinite metal credit card and lifestyle privileges.
4th Young Investors Programme (ages 18-25) closed: QSE simulation plus an international-market simulation on CB Alpha Trader.

Named Best Wealth Management Bank in Qatar at the TAB Global Middle East Awards 2026. The CEO says the advisory business has grown significantly over four years and the bank plans to broaden access to more sophisticated investment opportunities.
Senior appointments: Omran Al Sherawi as EGM Treasury and Investments, Nasser Al Harmi as Chief Human Capital Officer and Eiman Al-Naemi as Chief Communications and Marketing Officer.

2026-2030 strategy announced. Retail priorities: accelerate growth among Qatari affluent and Private Banking clients, deepen wealth and advisory relationships by expanding digital wealth tools, modernise core banking platforms, and use AI.
CBQ Mobile App adds investment account opening and wealth services, plus CB Video Relationship Manager. CBFS starts market-making. The group launches the Sondook money market fund.
Stephen Moss (ex-HSBC regional CEO MENAT) becomes Group CEO.

opportunities: The 2026-2030 strategy explicitly targets 'deepening wealth and advisory relationships through the expansion of digital wealth tools and solutions' and growth among affluent and Private Banking Qatari clients (S6 p.23).

The fund shelf (Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, Kotak) is sold through advisers. No model portfolios, robo service or in-app fund investing was found; the app opens investment accounts only (S12, S6).

The CEO said in Aug 2026 that the bank plans to broaden access to more sophisticated investment opportunities and strengthen advisory (S22). The website already lists 'Alternative Investments' as a product line (S14).
The investor presentation (H1 2026) lists core banking modernisation and enhanced digital onboarding and engagement across Retail, Wealth and Wholesale as strategic enablers (S8 p.5).
barriers: Has in-house investment manufacturing and execution: CBAM (QFCRA-licensed asset manager), CBFS (QSE broker and liquidity provider) and the proprietary CB Alpha Trader platform for international equities (S9, S17, S14).
New CEO (Aug 2025) and several 2026 executive changes (Treasury & Investments, COO, CHRO, CRO acting), with a core-banking modernisation programme competing for change budget (S1, S21, S8).
No wealth AUM or client numbers disclosed, so the size of the opportunity cannot be confirmed (S6, S8).
incumbent_vendors: Fidelity International, Franklin Templeton, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock and Kotak - fund distribution (S12)
WCP Investments - leasing and finance funds (2019; current status unclear) (S27)
